gold: Glioblastoma (World Health Organization grade IV) with optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension

selector.rationale: The presence of mutant IDH-1 protein and loss of ATRX protein in the vitreous biopsy, along with the hypercellular sample showing astrocytic neoplasm, supports the diagnosis of IDH-mutant Astrocytoma. The high Ki-67 proliferation index and positive immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acid protein and oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2 also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did experience vision loss and had findings consistent with central retinal artery occlusion, the underlying cause was likely the astrocytic neoplasm.

rejected.label: Astrocytic Neoplasm
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes IDH-mutant Astrocytoma, but the specific findings in this case support the more specific diagnosis of IDH-mutant Astrocytoma.

rejected.label: Glioblastoma
rejected.why: The presence of mutant IDH-1 protein and loss of ATRX protein, along with the relatively low Ki-67 proliferation index, make glioblastoma a less likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Glioma
rejected.why: While glioma is a possible diagnosis, the specific findings in this case support the more specific diagnosis of IDH-mutant Astrocytoma.
